pr_title: sql: restart rangefeed on descriptor table on error
pr_body:
Previously, if the rangefeed encountered a terminal error, it would remain offline. In at least one test, this led in our version check on drop to hang forever since it is the rangefeed that is responsible for driving the purging of leases on drop.

Now, we restart the feed.

Fixes #118625.
Informs #75610

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/119358)

I believe what is going on here is that this test sends a GCRequest that pushes the gc threshold to now(). That request, when run inside a tenant, includes the range for the leases system table. This can result in the rangefeed on the leases table failing. The lease code doesn't notice this and never restarts it. As a result, we never purge leases during a table drop, so we get stuck forever waiting on those leases during the schema change job. See also https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/75610. This seems like an accident waiting to happen. I think this is likely fixed by https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/126230 Based on the specified backports for linked PR #128577, I applied the following new label(s) to this issue: branch-release-24.1, branch-release-24.2. Please adjust the labels as needed to match the branches actually affected by this issue, including adding any known older branches. :owl: Hoot! I am a [Blathers](https://github.com/apps/blathers-crl), a bot for [CockroachDB](https://github.com/cockroachdb). My owner is [dev-inf](https://github.com/orgs/cockroachdb/teams/dev-inf).

review_comments: I think we probably need to do more than just restart the feed here. Namely, it would be nice to refresh our state in case we missed some update that would have resulted in us purging some leases.  I noted the refreshAllLeases channel, but some of the code led me to believe that perhaps that isn't what we want after we've moved to session based leases.  Wondering if someone from foundations might provide some guidance or pick this up. cc @fqazi
